# How to use this wiki

This wiki describes **HandOff247** for an AI assistant that has to answer questions about the project or change it. HandOff247 generated it by static analysis; it did not run the code and no language model wrote these pages.

## Reading

1. Start at [index.md](index.md). Open [overview.md](overview.md), then only the pages the question needs.
2. Each page is one thing. `Relations` lists what it points to (→) and what points to it (←); follow those links.
3. A `file:line` next to a statement is where it was observed. Open that source before you change code.
4. *inferred* marks a conclusion, not an observation. Check it in the source before relying on it.
   Text labelled *written by a language model* (and *(model)* in lists) was not checked by a person either.
5. Something that is not in the wiki was not found. That does not mean it does not exist: code built from runtime strings, reflection or dependency-injection containers is not followed. Say that you do not know.
6. [notes.md](notes.md) is the only human-written page. "Not answered" there is a question for a person.

## Classes

| Class | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Project | The thing being handed over. |
| Area | A top-level folder of the project. |
| File | A file of the project (images and other assets are left out). |
| Type | A class, record, struct, interface or enum defined in a file. |
| Run mode | A way to start the program, picked by its first argument. |
| Sub-command | A sub-command of a command-line parser. |
| Dispatch table | A switch or mapping that turns an operation name into the code that handles it. |
| Operation | One named operation of a dispatch table. |
| HTTP route | An HTTP endpoint the program serves. |
| MCP tool | A tool the program offers to AI clients over MCP. |
| Environment variable | An environment variable the code reads or sets (operating-system variables are left out). |
| Port | A network port number found in an address or a port setting. |
| Package | A third-party package the project declares or imports. |
| External host | A host name found in a URL. |
| Command-line tool | A well-known program the project's scripts start; it has to be installed. |
| Person | An author in the Git history. |

## Relations

| Relation | Read backwards | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| contains | is part of | Project → area → file. |
| defines | is defined in | The file holds the definition. |
| imports | is imported by | Import or include statement. |
| uses | is used by | The code names a type defined in the other file; a run mode uses a type. |
| takes as a dependency | is a dependency of | Constructor parameter of that type. |
| extends | is extended by | Base class or implemented interface. |
| loads | is loaded by | A page loads a script or stylesheet. |
| runs | is run by | A script or configuration starts the other file. |
| refers to | is referred to by | A string in the file is the other file's path. |
| references | is referenced by | Project reference in a build file. |
| documents | is documented in | A document links to the file or shows the operation in an example. |
| serves | is served by | A run mode passes requests to the dispatch table. |
| exposes | is exposed by | A run mode registers the HTTP route. |
| has operation | is an operation of | Key of the dispatch table. |
| is handled by | handles | The file that holds the handler the table calls. |
| calls | is called from | The file asks for the operation by name (over HTTP, a process or in-process). |
| invokes | is invoked by | An MCP tool runs the operation. |
| forwards to | receives from | An HTTP route hands the request to the dispatch table. |
| reads | is read by | The file reads the environment variable. |
| sets | is set by | The file sets the environment variable. |
| mentions | is mentioned in | The host or port appears in the file. |
| depends on | is a dependency of | The file declares or imports the package. |
| starts | is started by | The file starts the command-line tool. |
| has commits in | has commits by | Author in the Git history of the project. |

## Writing

Do not edit these pages: the next run overwrites them. Knowledge that should last goes into `HANDOFF.notes.md`, under the heading of the thing it is about:

- `## Project` — what the project is and its status
- `## Topic: <name>` — the handover questions listed in [notes.md](notes.md)
- `## Area: <folder>`, `## File: <path>`, `## Mode: <name>`, `## Op: <operation>` — one thing each

Write plain sentences, say only what you verified in the source, and never paste a password or token; say where it is kept. Then run `python -m handoff247 <project folder>` again: the note appears on the matching wiki page, in the handoff pages and in the viewer.

## Files

- `../llms.txt` — short entry point; `../llms-full.txt` — every page of this wiki in one file
- `../ontology.json` — entities (`id`, `type`, `name`, `summary`, `page`) and relations (`s`, `p`, `o`, `file`, `line`)
- `../index.html` — viewer with a graph of the same ontology

## Working through MCP

`python -m handoff247 mcp` is an MCP server over the same data: search and read entities, read source lines, list what is still undocumented, and write notes under the right heading (marked as written by an agent). It is the supported way for an assistant to add to this wiki.

# HandOff247

**What the previous owner says it is**

> HandOff247 reads a project folder and writes a handoff pack for the next person: diagrams, structure, extracted comments and a map of how the tools connect. It is static analysis only (it never imports or runs the target's code) and it is standard-library Python, so `python -m handoff247` works on any machine with Python 3.10+.
> Status: v0.5.0. `python -m handoff247 <folder>` does everything in one step (notes file, pack, handover checklist), and a folder that holds several projects gets one pack per project plus an index. Since v0.4.0 every pack also holds the ontology (`ontology.json`), a graph of it in the viewer, and a wiki for AI assistants (`wiki/`, `llms.txt`). v0.5.0 adds optional file summaries written through the signed-in Codex CLI (`--summarize`) and an MCP server (`handoff247 mcp`) through which an AI agent reads the project and writes notes. The first real target was PlayBookOS (see examples/playbookos). C#, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, PowerShell, shell and batch have analyzers; other languages are inventoried but not parsed. Output is English; a project's own comments and headings in another language get English versions from the notes file's `## Translations` table.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/unkkyuist/HandOff247 at commit `ffbe44f`
- **Human-readable pack:** [README](../README.md), [handover checklist](../HANDOVER.md), [how to run it](../RUNNING.md), [connections](../CONNECTIONS.md), [code map](../CODEMAP.md)
- **What only the previous owner knew:** [notes](notes.md)

<!-- page: wiki/notes.md -->

# Notes from the previous owner

Written by a person in `HANDOFF.notes.md`; nothing on this page was derived from code. A question without an answer is a real gap: ask, do not guess.

## What the project is

HandOff247 reads a project folder and writes a handoff pack for the next person: diagrams, structure, extracted comments and a map of how the tools connect. It is static analysis only (it never imports or runs the target's code) and it is standard-library Python, so `python -m handoff247` works on any machine with Python 3.10+.
Status: v0.5.0. `python -m handoff247 <folder>` does everything in one step (notes file, pack, handover checklist), and a folder that holds several projects gets one pack per project plus an index. Since v0.4.0 every pack also holds the ontology (`ontology.json`), a graph of it in the viewer, and a wiki for AI assistants (`wiki/`, `llms.txt`). v0.5.0 adds optional file summaries written through the signed-in Codex CLI (`--summarize`) and an MCP server (`handoff247 mcp`) through which an AI agent reads the project and writes notes. The first real target was PlayBookOS (see examples/playbookos). C#, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, PowerShell, shell and batch have analyzers; other languages are inventoried but not parsed. Output is English; a project's own comments and headings in another language get English versions from the notes file's `## Translations` table.

## Successor checklist

1. Run the tests: `python -m unittest discover -s tests`.
2. Regenerate the examples after any analyzer change: `python -m handoff247 build <PlayBookOS checkout> --name PlayBookOS -o examples/playbookos --notes examples/playbookos.notes.md --date <date>`. If an analyzer change surfaces new Korean comments or headings, `check --notes examples/playbookos.notes.md` reports them; add their rows to the Translations table there. Read the diff of the generated pages: a change there is a change in what successors will be told.
3. Regenerate this pack after committing and pushing, so its Handover page does not report your own work as uncommitted: `python -m handoff247 . --date <date>`.
4. Open `index.html` of a pack in a browser and check that every diagram renders (Mermaid errors show as red text in the page).

## Known issues and risks

- The rule that matters most: a wrong statement is worse than a missing one. When a pattern is ambiguous the analyzers leave it out; inferences (for example a wrapper passed in as a parameter) are labelled and drawn dashed. Keep it that way.
- Analysis is regex/lexer based for everything except Python (which uses `ast`). Code built from runtime strings, reflection or dependency-injection containers is not followed.
- MCP tool names from the C# SDK are derived from method names (snake_case, `Async` removed) and marked with * in the pack.
- Mermaid labels must go through `mermaid.esc`; `*`, `_` and backticks are escaped because Mermaid otherwise formats them as Markdown.

## Credentials and accounts

None. The tool needs no keys. The GitHub Action only uses the workflow's own checkout.

## Open work and next steps

- A folder of projects has a graph and a wiki per project but no single graph across projects; `workspace.py` only writes an `llms.txt` that links them.
- Codex is the only engine for `--summarize` (`summarize.codex_call`). Another signed-in CLI (Claude Code's `claude -p`, for example) would be a second function with the same signature: prompt in, JSON text out.
- The MCP server is tested by driving it over stdio (`test_mcp_server`) and was tried once by hand with Codex. It speaks protocol versions up to 2025-11-25 and offers tools only, no resources or prompts.
- Go, Rust, Java and other languages are only inventoried. An analyzer for one of them is the natural next piece: copy the shape of `analyzers/python.py` and add an assertion per fact to the tests.
- The workspace index has no example in `examples/`; it is covered by `test_go_folder_of_projects` only.

## Deploy and release

There is no server and no package upload. A release is a push to `main` on GitHub; people run it from a clone or use the repository as a GitHub Action (`uses: unkkyuist/HandOff247@main`), so `main` is what users get. Bump the version in `handoff247/__init__.py` and `pyproject.toml` together. To roll back, revert the commit.

## Routine operations

Nothing runs on a schedule. CI runs on every push and pull request. The viewer loads marked, DOMPurify and Mermaid from jsDelivr at pinned versions (`render_html.py`); check now and then that those versions still load.

## Data and backups

The tool stores nothing. Its only state is the Git repository. Generated packs can always be rebuilt; a project's `HANDOFF.notes.md` cannot, so it belongs in that project's repository.

## People and contacts

Owner: the GitHub account `unkkyuist` (issues on the repository). There are no other maintainers and no known outside users yet.

# `handoff247/cli.py`

> Four commands: `go`, `build`, `notes`, `check`. A first argument that is not a command is taken as a folder for `go`. `go` decides between one project and a folder of projects (`workspace.is_workspace`), then does notes…

- **Class:** File — A file of the project (images and other assets are left out).
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind of file:** code
- **Lines:** 219
- **Source:** [handoff247/cli.py](../../../../handoff247/cli.py)

**Notes from the previous owner**

> Four commands: `go`, `build`, `notes`, `check`. A first argument that is not a command is taken as a folder for `go`. `go` decides between one project and a folder of projects (`workspace.is_workspace`), then does notes + build + report. `check --min N` exits 1 when fewer than N% of files have notes, which is how CI can enforce documentation.

# `handoff247/connect.py`

> Turns per-file facts into edges and connection maps. The key idea: string keys of a dispatch table (`"list"`, `"ontology.search"`) are followed to every caller (`api('list')`, `cli('list')`, `Call("list")`, `cli list` i…

- **Class:** File — A file of the project (images and other assets are left out).
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind of file:** code
- **Lines:** 677
- **Source:** [handoff247/connect.py](../../../../handoff247/connect.py)

**Notes from the previous owner**

> Turns per-file facts into edges and connection maps. The key idea: string keys of a dispatch table (`"list"`, `"ontology.search"`) are followed to every caller (`api('list')`, `cli('list')`, `Call("list")`, `cli list` in docs), and each caller's wrapper function is inspected to tell HTTP, CLI process or in-process apart. A caller group only counts when it uses two or more keys or a dotted key, so ordinary strings like "git" are not mistaken for operations.

**defines** →

- `FileIndex` · [handoff247/connect.py:37](../../../../handoff247/connect.py#L37)

**imports** →

- [`handoff247/model.py`](handoff247__model.py.md) · [handoff247/connect.py:11](../../../../handoff247/connect.py#L11)

**is part of** ←

**is imported by** ←

- [`handoff247/notes.py`](handoff247__notes.py.md) · [handoff247/notes.py:15](../../../../handoff247/notes.py#L15)
- [`handoff247/ontology.py`](handoff247__ontology.py.md) · [handoff247/ontology.py:11](../../../../handoff247/ontology.py#L11)
- [`handoff247/pipeline.py`](handoff247__pipeline.py.md) · [handoff247/pipeline.py:7](../../../../handoff247/pipeline.py#L7)
- [`handoff247/render_md.py`](handoff247__render_md.py.md) · [handoff247/render_md.py:8](../../../../handoff247/render_md.py#L8)

## Comment in the file

Cross-file linking: turns per-file facts into edges and the connection maps (entry modes, dispatch tables and who calls each operation, routes, MCP tools, launch chain, environment variables, ports). *(module docstring)*

# `handoff247/leaving.py`

> The handover findings: Git state (uncommitted, commits on no remote, stashes, authors), files Git ignores that are present, absolute paths, hosts in URLs, TODO comments, key and token patterns, declared tool versions, a…

- **Class:** File — A file of the project (images and other assets are left out).
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind of file:** code
- **Lines:** 383
- **Source:** [handoff247/leaving.py](../../../../handoff247/leaving.py)

**Notes from the previous owner**

> The handover findings: Git state (uncommitted, commits on no remote, stashes, authors), files Git ignores that are present, absolute paths, hosts in URLs, TODO comments, key and token patterns, declared tool versions, and the readiness rows. Two rules to keep: a secret hit records file, line and kind but never the value, and anything that cannot be known is left out (no history figures for shallow clones, no "pushed" row without a remote). `JUNK_DIRS` decides which ignored folders are build output; add to it when a pack lists noise.

# `handoff247/mcp.py`

> The MCP server (`handoff247 mcp`): newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout, with `sys.stdout` pointed at stderr so stray prints cannot corrupt the protocol. Six tools; only `handoff_write_note` and `handoff_build` wr…

- **Class:** File — A file of the project (images and other assets are left out).
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind of file:** code
- **Lines:** 311
- **Source:** [handoff247/mcp.py](../../../../handoff247/mcp.py)

**Notes from the previous owner**

> The MCP server (`handoff247 mcp`): newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout, with `sys.stdout` pointed at stderr so stray prints cannot corrupt the protocol. Six tools; only `handoff_write_note` and `handoff_build` write. `handoff_write_note` accepts only skeleton headings (plus `Op:` for real operations), never overwrites filled text without `replace`, rejects key-like text and appends the agent mark. The analysed project is cached per folder and dropped after every write.

- [`handoff247/mcp.py:250`](../operations.md) · [handoff247/mcp.py:250](../../../../handoff247/mcp.py#L250)

# `handoff247/ontology.py`

> Turns `project.links` and `project.edges` into typed entities and relations. It detects nothing itself; add a new kind of fact in an analyzer or in `connect.py` first, then map it here. `CLASSES` and `RELATIONS` are the…

- **Class:** File — A file of the project (images and other assets are left out).
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind of file:** code
- **Lines:** 283
- **Source:** [handoff247/ontology.py](../../../../handoff247/ontology.py)

**Notes from the previous owner**

> Turns `project.links` and `project.edges` into typed entities and relations. It detects nothing itself; add a new kind of fact in an analyzer or in `connect.py` first, then map it here. `CLASSES` and `RELATIONS` are the schema: a class has a colour group and a shape (the graph has eight colours, so classes share one and differ by shape), a relation has a label for each direction. `_Builder.rel` drops a relation whose ends are not both entities, which is why assets and system environment variables never appear.

**imports** →

# `handoff247/render_html.py`

> The single-file viewer. It embeds the Markdown pages and loads marked, DOMPurify and Mermaid from jsDelivr at pinned versions. Diagram nodes are matched back to files through the `flowchart-nN-` element ids, so clicking…

- **Class:** File — A file of the project (images and other assets are left out).
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind of file:** code
- **Lines:** 537
- **Source:** [handoff247/render_html.py](../../../../handoff247/render_html.py)

**Notes from the previous owner**

> The single-file viewer. It embeds the Markdown pages and loads marked, DOMPurify and Mermaid from jsDelivr at pinned versions. Diagram nodes are matched back to files through the `flowchart-nN-` element ids, so clicking a node opens that file's card. The Graph tab is hand-written canvas code with no library: a force layout with a fixed seed (the same picture every run), hit testing, and names drawn most-connected first without overlap. The eight colours are the `--g1`…`--g8` variables; do not add a ninth, give a new class a shape inside an existing group. Wiki pages are embedded too, and `resolveHref` turns their page-relative links into pack-relative ones.

**imports** →

- [`handoff247/__init__.py`](handoff247____init__.py.md) · [handoff247/render_html.py:9](../../../../handoff247/render_html.py#L9)

**mentions** →

**is part of** ←

**is imported by** ←

# `handoff247/summarize.py`

> The optional `--summarize` step. It shells out to `codex exec` (read-only sandbox, empty temporary folder, `--ephemeral`, an output schema) with batches of files and their analysis facts, and keeps the answers in `<note…

- **Class:** File — A file of the project (images and other assets are left out).
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind of file:** code
- **Lines:** 325
- **Source:** [handoff247/summarize.py](../../../../handoff247/summarize.py)

**Notes from the previous owner**

> The optional `--summarize` step. It shells out to `codex exec` (read-only sandbox, empty temporary folder, `--ephemeral`, an output schema) with batches of files and their analysis facts, and keeps the answers in `<notes>.summaries.json` keyed by path with a content hash. Rules to keep: a file with a note is never sent; key-like lines are replaced with `[removed]` before sending (`redact`); answers for ids that were not asked for are dropped; a summary whose file hash no longer matches is ignored. `prepare()` is what the CLI and the workspace call before writing a pack.

**defines** →

- `EngineError` · [handoff247/summarize.py:57](../../../../handoff247/summarize.py#L57)

# `handoff247/translate.py`

> Finds extracted prose with letters outside the Latin script (summaries, doc comments, Markdown headings, MCP tool descriptions, sub-command help, commit subjects) and swaps in the English from the notes' Translations ta…

- **Class:** File — A file of the project (images and other assets are left out).
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind of file:** code
- **Lines:** 93
- **Source:** [handoff247/translate.py](../../../../handoff247/translate.py)

**Notes from the previous owner**

> Finds extracted prose with letters outside the Latin script (summaries, doc comments, Markdown headings, MCP tool descriptions, sub-command help, commit subjects) and swaps in the English from the notes' Translations table. Matching is exact apart from spacing, so a comment that changed later shows its original again instead of a stale translation. Identifiers such as file names are never touched.

# `handoff247/wiki.py`

> Writes the ontology as Markdown pages plus `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`. `assign_pages` decides which page describes an entity (own page for files, areas, modes, operations and MCP tools; a list page for the small cla…

- **Class:** File — A file of the project (images and other assets are left out).
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind of file:** code
- **Lines:** 391
- **Source:** [handoff247/wiki.py](../../../../handoff247/wiki.py)

**Notes from the previous owner**

> Writes the ontology as Markdown pages plus `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt`. `assign_pages` decides which page describes an entity (own page for files, areas, modes, operations and MCP tools; a list page for the small classes; a type lives on its file's page). File names are slugs with `/` as `__`; Windows reserved names get a `_` prefix. The pages are regenerated on every run, so durable knowledge belongs in the notes file; `agents()` is the page that tells an assistant so.

# `handoff247/workspace.py`

> The folder-of-projects mode: finds projects one or two levels down, builds a pack for each, and writes the index (README.md, index.html, workspace.json, workspace.mmd). It does not write into the projects: notes for a p…

- **Class:** File — A file of the project (images and other assets are left out).
- **Language:** Python
- **Kind of file:** code
- **Lines:** 350
- **Source:** [handoff247/workspace.py](../../../../handoff247/workspace.py)

**Notes from the previous owner**

> The folder-of-projects mode: finds projects one or two levels down, builds a pack for each, and writes the index (README.md, index.html, workspace.json, workspace.mmd). It does not write into the projects: notes for a project without its own notes file go to `<out>/notes/`. One failing project is listed as failed and the rest continue. Cross-project arrows come only from paths that resolve into another project's folder.
